title: sdks: auth/retries + streaming parity and ergonomics bump v1.69.0
author: Jordan White
release_notes: Python/TS/Go SDKs: unify auth retry behavior, streaming API ergonomics improvements, parity fixes, and version bumps to v1.69.0. Bugfixes: token refresh race, transient 401 retries, streaming reconnect stability. Backwards-compatible changes only.
description: Motivation: Multiple customers and internal e2e tests surfaced flaky token refreshes and inconsistent retry semantics across SDKs, and ergonomics mismatches in streaming APIs between Python/TS/Go. This PR consolidates auth+retry logic, improves streaming ergonomics (resume tokens, client-side reconnect/backoff), fixes parity gaps, and bumps SDK versions to v1.69.0. Summary of changes: 1) Centralized auth retry middleware across SDKs: uniform exponential backoff with jitter, capped retries for 401/403 during token refresh, and clear error surfaces when refresh fails. 2) Streaming ergonomics: Python and TS clients now expose a single StreamClient abstraction with unified on_message/on_error/on_close hooks, improved reconnect logic, and resume_token support for short interruptions. Go client receives parity methods and a simplified Receive(ctx) that returns a typed event stream. 3) Hotfixes: race in Python token cache leading to double-refresh, TS incremental backpressure bug causing lost messages under load, Go streaming hang when server resets connection. 4) Docs and examples updated: quickstarts for streaming reconnect and retry configuration. 5) Version bumps: python v1.69.0, typescript v1.69.0, go v1.69.0. Checklist: - [x] Central auth retry middleware implemented for python/typescript/go - [x] Streaming API ergonomics consolidated for python/typescript/go - [x] Unit tests added/adjusted - [x] Integration tests in perf-canary updated - [x] Changelog and release notes updated - [x] Manual QA on staging passed Notes: This is intended to be backwards-compatible; existing call patterns still work but new ergonomics recommended. If downstream users rely on internal token-refresh timing they should read the updated auth docs.
